preamble: Total assimilation of the coda tap [ɾ] to a following [m], giving a geminate [mm]. In western Cuban Spanish (the provinces from Pinar del Río to Matanzas and Cienfuegos, including Havana, plus the municipalities of Corralillo and Trinidad), coda /ɾ/ and coda /l/ merge and assimilate to the next consonant; before /m/ both surface as [m], so arma 'weapon' is pronounced a[mm]a, the same as alma 'soul'. The assimilation also applies across word boundaries (dar migas > da[mm]igas). The unassimilated pronunciations remain more common. The trill r shows the same total assimilation in Middle Indo-Aryan (Sanskrit karman > Pali kamma), filed under r > m.

examples.note: Homophonous with alma 'soul', because coda /l/ assimilates in the same way (Arias 2019, also cited on the Cuban Spanish and Caribbean Spanish Wikipedia pages).
Arias contrasts it with das migas, pronounced da[hm]igas, where coda /s/ is aspirated instead.

Arias (2019) analyses the merged coda liquid as a new unit /d/, realized [d] before a pause (ve[d] 'ver', ma[d] 'mar'), and assigns its realizations before /m/ and /n/ to the nasal phoneme /n/, because they are identical to those of /n/ (da[mm]inutos for both dar minutos and dan minutos).

sources: Arias Cabal, Á. (2019). Fonética y fonología de las consonantes geminadas en el español de Cuba. Moenia, 25, 465–497. https://revistas.usc.gal/index.php/moenia/article/view/6474
